questions.q: What does the Sharing Settings page in Setup actually contain?
options: OWD per object, sharing rules, and org-wide toggles like guest user record access, all in one place
Only the org-wide default settings
Only field-level security settings
A list of all users and their passwords
questions.explain: The page is the home for OWD, sharing rules, and several org-wide access toggles — the single screen view of the org's record-access model.

questions.q: Why does Salesforce maintain precomputed 'sharing tables' instead of recalculating access on every click?
options: Sharing tables are required for field-level security to function
Because sharing rules cannot be evaluated in real time at all
So that opening a record or running a report doesn't have to re-derive the full OWD/hierarchy/sharing-rule chain every time
To store user passwords securely
questions.explain: Precomputing access into sharing tables keeps everyday record access fast, instead of re-evaluating the whole access chain on every single page load.

questions.q: Which of these typically triggers sharing recalculation automatically, with no admin action needed?
options: Editing the company logo
Renaming a custom field's label
Changing a user's email signature
A user's role changing or a record's ownership changing
questions.explain: Ordinary day-to-day changes like role changes and ownership changes trigger automatic recalculation in the background.

questions.q: Why can a large sharing recalculation take minutes to hours for a big org?
options: Salesforce artificially delays recalculation to save server costs
It's a background job that walks every affected record and reevaluates access, which scales with data volume and hierarchy depth
Recalculation always takes exactly 24 hours regardless of org size
It only runs once per year
questions.explain: The job has real work to do — reevaluating every affected record against the current model — so its duration scales with how much data and hierarchy complexity exist.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend not testing a large OWD or hierarchy change immediately after making it?
options: Because access may still reflect the old sharing model until recalculation finishes, which can look like the change failed
Because testing is never useful after a security change
Because Login As is disabled during recalculation
Because testing immediately would corrupt the sharing tables
questions.explain: During the recalculation window, old access still applies — testing too soon can produce confusing, seemingly-stale results that aren't actually a sign the change didn't work.
